In front of an online audience of thousands last Thursday, OpenAI’s head recruiter, Joaquin Quiñonero Candela, described one of the common threads that draws talent to the company: OpenAI’s culture.“We’re a culture of doers who do things – with autonomy, with agency,” he said at the OpenAI Forum. “There’s no sitting around asking for permission.”Joaquin also mentioned how OpenAI’s mission is attractive to candidates. “We’re building AGI, and we’re bringing it to humanity in a way that’s responsible and beneficial.” And he explained how it’s the people at OpenAI who draw talent to the company. “We often say good people draw good people. New Anthropic research: How university students use Claude.We ran a privacy-preserving analysis of a million education-related conversations to produce our first Education Report.Our findings show students primarily use Claude to create and improve educational content (39.3%) and provide technical explanations (33.5%).Computer Science dominates AI usage, representing 38.6% of Claude conversations despite making up only 5.4% of US degrees.We created a taxonomy for how students interact with AI, and tracked how common those interaction styles were across different subjects. Science and Math saw more Collaborative Problem Solving; Education saw more Direct Output Creation.Our taxonomy reveals distinct interaction patterns: more Collaborative Problem Solving in Science/Math and Direct Output Creation in Education fields.We also wondered, are students using AI to cheat?It’s hard to know whether any specific category is cheating or legitimate study, but we did notice some concerning patterns: students straightforwardly asking for answers, or asking Claude to rewrite an essay to avoid plagiarism detection.Students mostly used AI to create and analyze, according to our analysis using Bloom’s Taxonomy of educational goals.Whether cheating or not, this raises important questions about how to stop students offloading important cognitive tasks to AI. AI can empower learning in remarkable ways. But we’re under no illusions that all the changes it’s bringing to education are positive.Our research will help educators and policymakers ensure that AI deepens, rather than undermines, learning.Read the full report:https://lnkd.in/eABqfPtaWe’re working with universities to help realize the benefits of AI.
